source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A pregnant woman hyperventilates and feels tingling and light-headedness. What should the nurse advise?
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation causes respiratory alkalosis; rebreathing through a paper bag or cupped hands helps.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Changes (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Breathe through a paper bag or through cupped hands.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A pregnant woman craves and eats clay. What is this?
questions.rationale: Pica is an appetite for non-nutritive substances such as clay, chalk, or soil.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 193)
questions.quote: Medical disorder characterized by an appetite for substances largely non-nutritive

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How is gum swelling and bleeding (epulis) in pregnancy managed?
questions.rationale: Epulis is from increased estrogen; use a soft brush and avoid strong mouthwash.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which advice helps heartburn in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Small frequent meals, avoiding supine position after eating, and gradual ambulation help.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, GI Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why are pregnant women prone to UTI?
questions.rationale: Hormone-induced relaxation of the renal pelvis and ureters causes urine stagnation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Renal Changes (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: relaxation of renal pelvis and the ureter leading to urine stagnation

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which hormone loosens the pelvic joints in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: Relaxin from the placenta relaxes pelvic joints.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Musculoskeletal Changes (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: Placenta can produce the hormone, relaxin

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which measure relieves back pain from pregnancy lordosis?
questions.rationale: Pelvic rocking and lumbar pressure help; avoid supine position.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Musculoskeletal Changes (PDF p. 194)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Why are NSAIDs such as indomethacin avoided late in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: NSAIDs can close the ductus arteriosus prematurely and reduce fetal urine, causing oligohydramnios.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Drugs in Pregnancy (PDF p. 194)
questions.quote: Causes premature closure of the Ductus Arteriosus

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: What should the woman do before amniocentesis?
questions.rationale: Voiding reduces bladder size and prevents accidental puncture; observe 30 minutes after.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Amniotic fluid over 1200 mL is called:
questions.rationale: Normal 800–1200 mL; oligohydramnios under 500 mL; polyhydramnios over 1200 mL.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Green-tinged amniotic fluid suggests:
questions.rationale: Green suggests meconium; strong yellow suggests blood incompatibility.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which L:S ratio indicates fetal lung maturity?
questions.rationale: A lecithin:sphingomyelin ratio of 2:1 indicates lung maturity.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Amniocentesis (PDF p. 195)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: How is a woman prepared for a TRANSABDOMINAL ultrasound early in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: A full bladder pushes the uterus up for better view; transvaginal needs voiding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ultrasound (PDF p. 196)
questions.quote: Ask the client to drink plenty of water 1 hour before procedure.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: A 'snowstorm' pattern on first-trimester ultrasound suggests:
questions.rationale: H-mole shows a snowstorm appearance of fluid-filled vesicles.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ultrasound (PDF p. 196)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: A biophysical profile score of 8–10 means:
questions.rationale: BPP 8–10 normal; 6 suspicious; 4 jeopardy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Biophysical Score (PDF p. 196)
questions.quote: Fetal score of 8-10= fetus is doing well

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which NST result is REACTIVE (normal)?
questions.rationale: Reactive NST: two or more accelerations of 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds with movement in 20 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-Stress Test (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: Two or more accelerations of fetal heart rate of 15 beats/min lasting 15 seconds

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which contraction stress test result is NORMAL?
questions.rationale: A negative CST has no late decelerations with contractions; positive (late decels) is abnormal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Contraction Stress Test (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: Negative (Normal): No late decelerations with contractions

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Late decelerations appear during an oxytocin challenge test. What is FIRST?
questions.rationale: Turn left lateral, stop oxytocin, give O2 8–10 L/min, and hydrate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Contraction Stress Test (PDF p. 197)
questions.quote: Stop oxytocin immediately: no contractions wanted.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: An ELEVATED maternal serum AFP suggests:
questions.rationale: Elevated AFP suggests neural tube defects; decreased suggests chromosomal disorders like Down syndrome.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alpha-fetoprotein (PDF p. 197)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: When is chorionic villi sampling done?
questions.rationale: CVS is done at 8–10 weeks; amniocentesis at 14–16 weeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Chorionic Villi Sampling (PDF p. 197)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: The main psychological task in the SECOND trimester is:
questions.rationale: First trimester: accept pregnancy; second: accept the baby; third: accept parenthood.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Psychological Tasks (PDF p. 198)
questions.quote: Acceptance of the baby is the main task

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which pelvis type is ideal for childbirth?
questions.rationale: The gynecoid pelvis is the normal female pelvis with a well-rounded inlet.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pelvic Dimension (PDF p. 198)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: The presenting part is at the level of the ischial spines. What is the station?
questions.rationale: Station 0 (engaged) is at the ischial spines; minus is above, plus is below; +3 is crowning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fetal Station (PDF p. 199)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: When does the posterior fontanelle close?
questions.rationale: The triangular posterior fontanelle closes at 2–3 months; the anterior at 12–18 months.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fetal Head (PDF p. 199)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: Which finding indicates TRUE labor?
options: Pain only in the lower abdomen
questions.rationale: True labor has regular, intensifying contractions starting in the back with progressive dilation and effacement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, True vs False Labor (PDF p. 200)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: In a primigravida, lightening usually occurs:
questions.rationale: Lightening occurs about 2 weeks before labor in primigravidas and at labor in multigravidas.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preliminary Signs of Labor (PDF p. 199)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother During Labor and Birth
questions.stem: During which phase of labor is dilation 8–10 cm with contractions every 2–3 minutes?
questions.rationale: Transition: 8–10 cm, strongest contractions lasting 60–90 seconds every 2–3 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stages of Labor (PDF p. 200)
